title: Add guided multi-account setup and evaluation
body:
> [Prototype overview and documentation](https://cli.github.io/multi-account-docs/)
>
> **DO NOT MERGE.** This stack is almost entirely vibe coded. These drafts are for handy review and prototyping, not merging as-is.
>
> Expect the code to be really bad in places: highly coupled, handling edge cases that do not really matter, or doing suspiciously fragile things like parsing GraphQL request bodies.
>
> I suspect some of the suspicious code also exposes the complexity of this feature set, because account selection, Git configuration, scope precedence, worktrees, SSH and API requests all interact.
>
> The prototype experience is the purpose, not the code. I want to find out whether the experience is useful, not defend this implementation or treat it as a design to preserve.

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the

Follow on from https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14926

Evaluating persistent authentication changes needs a clear setup path and a way to isolate the experiment. This PR adds guided setup, developer evaluation tools and debug-only keyring isolation.

Layer 8 of an eight-part prototype review stack. This is a way to review the design and implementation in smaller pieces, not a proposal to merge the current stack as-is.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual

hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.

I exercised the debug keyring-isolation capability and reset in disposable configuration. I read the actual global and managed files before reset, then saw the user include remain and authenticated with the retained real account.

```text
$ cat ~/.gitconfig; cat ~/.ordinary.gitconfig
[include]
	path = /Users/Shared/gc-H8vKqb/r-5aVX8u/home/.ordinary.gitconfig
[user]
	name = Ordinary Author
	email = ordinary@example.invalid
```

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

This layer adds evaluation and setup tooling, not a new identity storage format. The reset recording exercises cleanup already available in the stack so reviewers can see how to return to ordinary configuration.

Live evaluation tools are optional and can create GitHub resources. The offline review scripts use synthetic accounts and deny network and Keychain access. Real-account recordings are separate from those scripts.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

Start with the setup approval boundaries, then isolation and cleanup. The guided-agent workflow and full live acceptance runner were not exercised for these recordings. Reset managed configuration before removing a prerelease executable referenced by Git.

The recordings use the product code at this layer, not a later stack endpoint. The included offline replay scripts are supplementary and do not reproduce the live-account recordings.

<details><summary>Offline replay on macOS</summary>

Build this layer, then run its synthetic scenario with an absolute executable path. This is a replay instruction, not a claim that the command below was used to make the videos.

```sh
make
env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin \
  /bin/bash script/multiaccount-review/08-reset.sh --gh "$PWD/bin/gh" --stable-gh /absolute/path/to/stable/gh
```

</details>

### Acceptance Criteria

Prototype behaviour under review:

**Given** a developer explicitly chooses to evaluate the prototype.

**When** the isolated workflow is used and the experiment is reset.

**Then** managed identity wiring is removed while ordinary user configuration and saved accounts remain.
